title: From hiding, Joseph orders witnessed records of baptisms for the dead
setting: In August 1842 Joseph Smith faced arrest and possible extradition to Missouri. Former Missouri governor Lilburn Boggs and John Bennett had accused him of a part in an attempt on Boggs’s life. Joseph hid with friends in and near Nauvoo and across the river in Iowa Territory. On 1 September he dictated this letter to William Clayton. It was read to the Saints in the grove near the temple site on 4 September. Baptisms for the dead had been performed since 1840, and the temple font was dedicated in November 1841.
summary: Joseph Smith writes to the Saints explaining why he has left home for a time. He says enemies in Missouri and Illinois pursue him without just cause. He has left his business with agents and will return when the storm passes. He says danger has been his lot all his life, yet God has always delivered him. A revelation then tells the Saints to continue the temple work with redoubled diligence. It directs that a recorder witness every baptism for the dead, so what is recorded on earth may be recorded in heaven. The records are to be kept in order in the temple. Joseph closes, unable to speak in person, and promises more letters.

contextNote.title: Why a witness must see and hear
contextNote.text: Baptisms for the dead had been performed for two years, with records that varied in detail. Verse 6 now asks for a recorder who sees and hears each baptism. Verse 7 gives the reason: so that “in all your recordings it may be recorded in heaven”. The same verse links the earthly record to binding on earth and in heaven. Verse 8 explains the timing: the Lord is “about to restore many things” about priesthood. Verse 9 adds that the records must be kept in order in the temple archives. In this passage, a careful record is part of the ordinance itself, not an afterthought.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 125–128 uses verses 2–4 to teach reliance on the Lord in hard times. What does Joseph call “a second nature” in verse 2, and how does verse 4 turn that into direction for the Saints?

jsp.title: Letter to “All the Saints in Nauvoo,” 1 September 1842 [D&C 127]

reviewNote: Read all 12 verses. Official heading gives an epistle dated 1 September 1842 at Nauvoo, written while Joseph was away for his safety. JSP historical introduction read: dictated to William Clayton; Joseph in hiding in and near Nauvoo and in Iowa Territory; letter apparently passed by Erastus Derby to Clayton and read on 4 September; baptisms for the dead since August 1840 and font dedicated 8 November 1841. JSP says it is unclear exactly when and where the letter was finalized. The Boggs accusation detail comes from a JSP footnote. Bennett is in personIds from the setting, not named in the text.
